source.title: Decreasing scaling transition from adaptive gradient descent to stochastic gradient descent
source.authors: Kun Zeng; Jin-Lan Liu; Zhixia Jiang; Dongpo Xu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; some figure content is garbled, but the results are described in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers and SGD, and tests a transition method using CIFAR test accuracy, a different optimizer recipe aimed at the same generalization comparison.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10/100 comparisons report test accuracy for four optimizers. The cited prior studies are not this paper's results. Training-loss and learning-rate-distribution descriptions are omitted because they do not directly measure the claim's test-error gap.
record.test_reason: The CIFAR experiments test V4's transition-recipe qualification: gradually transitioning Adam toward SGD improves held-out accuracy relative to both Adam and SGDM. The supplied text does not establish the direct Adam-versus-SGDM ordering.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that DSTAdam provides a smooth, stable transition from Adam to SGD and combines fast convergence with good generalization on CIFAR-10/100. They also prove an online convex regret bound, which does not itself establish held-out generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a decreasing-scaling transition from Adam to SGD; compares it with separate SGDM, Adam and AdaBound runs. Uses ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10/100 for 200 epochs at batch size 128.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the reported comparison: CIFAR-10 has about 1% improvement over other algorithms, while CIFAR-100 is described qualitatively as slightly better than AdaBound and better than SGDM and Adam.
record.problems: Only ResNet-18 image-classification experiments are reported. Test-accuracy comparisons are largely shown in plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates; the text gives only approximate or qualitative comparisons.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its relationship to natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Broader tuning removing optimizer differences, decoupled weight decay, language benchmarks, and abrupt switching. A direct Adam-versus-SGDM generalization disadvantage is indeterminate in the supplied figures. Comparator learning rates use fixed settings; only DSTAdam's additional learning-rate endpoints receive a reported grid search.
Batch-size effects and remedies under fixed epoch budgets.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. Its transition results bear on an explicit qualification in V4, but do not independently establish Adam's disadvantage relative to SGDM. Comparisons use the same random seed; uncertainty across runs is not reported.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Image-classification results are reported, but the paper does not evaluate broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching mid-training, or language models.
Large-batch comparisons and fixed-epoch batch-size effects.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other gap-tracking measures.
